articles.text: ant to us, because how we’re calculating attendance could be challenging come fall. So we’re very grateful that we’ll have a 19-20 hold harness provision,” Booker explained. At a June 30 special meeting, School board member Cory Smegal noted that “there needs to be major structural changes to our distance learning models, should we continue to use them next year,” based on feedback received from parents throughout the Spring semester. Families may choose a 100 percent distance learning model for their individual child or children. Booker added that there will be a strong need for substitute teaching pools, and will call on community members in the future to fill that pool. Booker recommended a daily bell schedule that offers in-person instruction to the greatest extent possible under the blended learning model. Under AB77, daily attendance must be taken, in remote learning and in person learning settings. At the end of a six-week period, if prescribed by the Board of Education and developed benchmarks, schools may return to a full in-person learning model. “Any plan that we develop today or in a couple of days, may need to be readdressed in a short period of time due to current conditions,” Booker said at the June 30 meeting. “We are asking the community to take social distancing measures very seriously, and that families should be wearing masks. As we come into the fall with our students and staff, it will be a main component of our programs.” Health & safety recommendations Booker made health and safety recommendations to the board when considering a blended model of instruction. This would include spacing desks at least six feet apart, staggering students in areas of high traffic, mark six-foot boundaries within classrooms, common areas, dining areas, and place students may gather, and utilizing restroom stalls in a manner that would allow for social distancing. The district would also determine specific entrances and exits at each campus for student classes to minimize large gatherings. Rallies, field trips, and assemblies would be suspended. “These are all strategies to ensure as much social distancing as we can perform,” Booker said. All employees and students would be required to wear face coverings while on district campuses. The district has already secured “an ample supply of KN95 masks for staff and non-surgical masks for students,” Booker explained. The National Palace Museum, Taipei, Taiwan The National Palace Museum began as the former Palace Museum in the Forbidden City, whose collection included artwork from the Ming and Qing dynasties. The permanent collection features nearly 700,000 pieces of imperial artifacts and encompasses 8,000 years of Chinese history. These include pieces of calligraphic works by Tang Yin. The National Palace Museum compound also includes classic Chinese Song and Ming-style Zhishan Garden. To see what the museum has to offer online, visit https://www. npm.gov.tw/en/. Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa, Cape Town, South Africa The Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA) is a contemporary art museum located at the V&A Waterfront in Cape Town, South Africa. It is the largest museum of contemporary African art in the world. The museum opened in 2017 and has since garnered the title of one of the most visited art museums in Africa. With the help of design firm Heatherwick Studio, a century-old grain silo complex in the heart of Cape Town was transformed into Zeitz MOCAA, now a 100-gallery museum of 21st century art from Africa and its diaspora. To learn more about Zeitz MOCAA, visit their website at https://zeitzmocaa.museum/. As we come into the fall with our students and staff, it will be a main component of our programs.” Health & safety recommendations Booker made health and safety recommendations to the board when considering a blended model of instruction. This would include spacing desks at least six feet apart, staggering students in areas of high traffic, mark six-foot boundaries within classrooms, common areas, dining areas, and place students may gather, and utilizing restroom stalls in a manner that would allow for social distancing. The district would also determine specific entrances and exits at each campus for student classes to minimize large gatherings. Rallies, field trips, and assemblies would be suspended. “These are all strategies to ensure as much social distancing as we can perform,” Booker said. All employees and students would be required to wear face coverings while on district campuses. The district has already secured “an ample supply of KN95 masks for staff and non-surgical masks for students,” Booker explained. articles.text: • The American Red Cross strongly urges healthy, eligible individuals who are feeling well to give blood or platelets to help maintain a sufficient blood supply and prevent shortages as concerns about the outbreak of coronavirus disease 2019, or COVID-19, rise in the U.S. Cold and f lu season has already impacted the nation’s ability to maintain its blood supply. As the number of coronavirus cases grows in the U.S., the number of people eligible to give blood for patients in need could decrease further. “We’re asking people to help keep the blood supply stable during this challenging time. As communities across the country prepare for this public health emergency, it’s critical that plans include a readily available blood supply for hospital patients,” said Chris Hrouda, president of Red Cross Blood Services. “As fears of coronavirus rise, low donor participation could harm blood availability at hospitals, and the last thing a patient should worry about is whether lifesaving blood will be on the shelf when they need it most.” including wearing gloves, routinely wiping down donortouched areas, using sterile collection sets for every donation, and preparing the arm for donation with an aseptic scrub. These mitigation measures will help ensure blood recipient safety, as well as staff and donor safety in reducing contact with those who may potentially have this respiratory infection. The Red Cross has implemented new blood donation deferrals out of an abundance of caution. Individuals are asked to postpone their donation for 28 days following: • Travel to China and its special administrative regions, Hong Kong and Macau, as well as Iran, Italy and South Korea; Diagnosis of COVID-19, contact with a person who has or is suspected to have the virus. As the situation evolves, the Red Cross will continue to evaluate all emerging risks in collaboration with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and industry partners to determine if additional intervention strategies are needed. Together, we stand ready to keep the American public informed and prepared. Blood donation process A blood donation takes about an hour from start to finish, but the actual donation itself only takes about 8-10 minutes. Donors can also save up to 15 minutes at the blood drive by completing a RapidPass®. With RapidPass®, donors complete the pre-donation reading and health history questionnaire online, on the day of donation, from a mobile device or computer. To complete a RapidPass®, follow the instructions at RedCrossBlood.org/RapidPass or use the Red Cross Blood Donor App. To donate blood, individuals need to bring a blood donor card or driver’s license or two other forms of identification that are required at check-in. Individuals who are 17 years of age in most states (16 with parental consent where allowed by state law), weigh at least 110 pounds and are in generally good health may be eligible to donate blood. High school students and other donors 18 years of age and younger also must meet certain height and weight requirements. Oakland Blood Donation Center, 6230 Claremont Avenue. Call 510-547-6456 for hours. Make an appointment to donate blood now by using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting RedCrossBlood.org, or calling the Oakland Blood Donation Center, 6230 Claremont Avenue, at 510-658-6456. Donating blood is a safe process and people should not hesitate to give or receive blood. There are no data or evidence that this coronavirus can be transmissible by blood transfusion, and there have been no reported cases worldwide of transmissions for any respiratory virus, including this coronavirus, from a transfusion. The Red Cross only collects blood from individuals who are healthy and feeling well at the time of donation – and who meet other eligibility requirements, available at RedCrossBlood.org. At each blood drive and donation center, Red Cross employees follow thorough safety protocols CROSSWORD SOLUTION

articles.text: on behalf of the disgruntled populace – “Dear Holy One. We want your attention when we want it and how we want it. Anything less will result in a tantrum of epic proportions.” The prophets inveighed against the construction and worship of idols. These distracted from the worship of the One God who alone was worthy of respect. These were invitations to forget the One God’s resolute commitment to justice, care for the downtrodden and concern for the well-being of widows and orphans. The Roman Emperor’s visage on a coin was problematic to Jesus and his contemporaries. Jesus acknowledged that there wasn’t much he could do to undo this act of arrogant grandiosity, but he refused to be subservient to the Emperor. His words were, “Give to Caesar that which is Caesar’s, but reserve for God that which is God’s.” In a profoundly inhumane manner, the Roman Empire erected the crucified as temporary statues. Statues to the power of the state. Statues warning against insurrection. Statues declaring who it was that deserved to be treated as human and who did not. Statues that stood sentinel against dreams of a better day for the people of the land. The word statue comes to us from Latin via Old French. It has to do with that which is represented in metal, and that which is set up. This etymology reminds us that statues have a history. They do not spontaneously evolve in a particular time, in a particular place, in a particular way. They are made. They are set up. They are created to send a message. The message statues send is often problematic. The Bible understands this. Hence, its caution in their regard. The Bible understands that human beings are very complex, that our motives are often less than pure. Thus, it urges us to be very careful about how we enshrine ourselves, how we tell our story. Rev. Jim Hopkins is Pastor of Lakeshore Avenue Baptist Church, 3534 Lakeshore Avenue at Mandana Blvd, in Oakland.

articles.text: On Wednesday June 24 at 2 p.m. a man in his late twenties walked into Mulberry’s Market without wearing a mask. He began talking nonsensically to a manager and then became unruly and angry at the counter. Mulberry’s General Manager Sal Viveros stepped in and told him multiple times that he needed to leave if he refused to comply with the State of California order to wear a mask. The man jumped towards Viveros and punched him. Two staff members behind the counter quickly pulled the man off of the manager and got him down to the ground. On his way down to the floor, the suspect grabbed a bottle off a display and tried to smash it on the employees. He ended up breaking the bottle and cutting his own hand. The cut spilled quite a bit of blood onto the floor. Two staff members held him down until the police got there about 90 seconds later. The police determined that he required medical attention and was taken to the hospital. He was cited for vandalism, assault and a health violation. Mulberry’s intends to press charges.

articles.text: Four years ago the Romona-Ronada neighborhood kids entered their float into the Piedmont Fourth of July parade for the eleventh and final year. The four organizers of the float were heading off to college, hence the name of their float “Aloha, Piedmont.” Decorated with surfboards and beach balls, their float won the Highland cup for best entry and the award for Most Artistic.

pages.text: 32 Wednesday, July 1, 2020 4th of July Continued from page 1 will be plenty of fun to be had even while staying safe. “Activities in front of homes are key to getting neighbors to know one another and are a way for strangers walking by to become friends. And of course, all of this can be accomplished while remaining socially distant and safe!” Former Piedmont Middle School Principal John Morrison, a longtime parade committee member and the person in charge of all the cars, will miss the camaraderie with the other members of the Bay Area Horseless Carriage Club for pre-1916 cars; but he will still be on the lookout for vehicular displays of patriotism and creativity this year as a judge in the contest. “There are quite a few cars from the parade that will be on display in Piedmont,” he confirmed. “It will be fun to drive around to look at them all dressed-up in their driveways.” The theme this year is Celebrating in Place. Traditional red, white and blue decorations will be aplenty, but new creative ideas have been formulating in Piedmonters’ minds during the Shelter in Place. Consider decorating your front yard with crepe paper, emulating a favorite vacation locale, supporting the changing social climate, honoring health care workers, staging scenes with hazmat suits or just putting masks on everything. While casual participants are widely encouraged, all official entries for judging are due by 5:00 p.m. tomorrow, Thursday, July 2. Judging will begin on July 3 at 4:00 p.m. and will continue until the parade committee and judges have visited all locations of individuals who submitted entry forms. See a sample entry form in today’s Post. To enter, send in a contact name, group name, the date, address, phone number, email and group description. Entries should be sent to Parade Commission Chair Carla Betts by e-mail to carlabetts@hotmail.com.
